newsitem.title: GERMANY: Escada expects level profit in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: Escada expects level profit in 96/97.

text.p: German women's clothing group Escada AG said on Wednesday it expected level pretax profit and a modest group sales rise in the 1996/97 business year.
The company expected a single-digit growth rate for sales this year, which ends October 31. Profit should reach the level of 1995/96, although the company did not rule out a decline.
Escada said restructuring costs in foreign units would keep profit from rising this year.

It expected to see positive effects its exchange rate hedging activities and the strong dollar at the beginning of the 1997/98 business year -- either in improved profit margins or stronger competitiveness.
Escada also planned to refinance short-term bank credits to take advantage of favourable interest rates.

Earlier on Monday, Escada reported 1995/96 group sales rose five percent to 1.23 billion marks, while net profit climbed 14.5 percent to 32.3 million marks. Operating profit rose four percent to 31.9 million marks last year.
The company also said it would hold 1995/96 dividends level at six marks per common share and seven marks per preferred share.
